Freefield

Open-source Higgsfield on ComfyUI: every app is one folder, every model is open weights.

 Watch the 2-minute demo video 

 

Image, video, VFX and audio apps in a studio laid out like Higgsfield's, each one a ComfyUI workflow on open weights,
run on Modal, on a GPU rented by the hour (RunPod, Vast.ai) or on your own ComfyUI. Every example in the app is a real GPU run made by the lab, with its time and peak VRAM.

Run it on RunPod or Vast.ai, on Modal or on your own PC in one line · every app with its model and VRAM · add an app from any ComfyUI workflow ·
every GPU run of the lab

 
 
 Explore. Featured apps, the studios, and one lab example per app. 
 An app. The form is drawn from the app's app.json ; "Load this example" fills it with a lab run. 
 
 
 The Video menu. 46 apps grouped as in Higgsfield, and the open models behind them. 
 How it works. Every model with its size and license, the VRAM per phase, and the commands to run the app. 
 
 

Freefield rebuilds Higgsfield's creative apps (image, video, VFX, audio) on top of ComfyUI and the Comfy SDK.
There is no per-app code. Each app is a folder in apps/ with an app.json manifest and a ComfyUI workflow in API
format; the web UI, the runner, the model downloads, the VRAM map and the tests are all derived from those manifests.

 

 

 Sponsors

Freefield runs open-weights models on your own GPU and stays free. Sponsors help keep it going; their text is their own.

Stop overpaying for AI: up to 99% off official API prices. 100% genuine models for text, image and video, one API key.
Freefield users: get CNY 5 free through this link. 
 
 

 One click on RunPod or Vast.ai

No install and no Modal account. Rent a GPU with Freefield's public template: it starts the backend and the studio,
prints a link to open, and downloads the models of the default packs (64 apps, 22.9 GB) while the studio shows how it
goes.

 Deploy on RunPod Rent on Vast.ai 
 --- --- --- 
 1. Hugging Face token (once, optional: accept the FLUX 3 license first; without it, the studio asks) Settings → Secrets → hf token , with your read token Account → Environment Variables → HF TOKEN 
 2. GPU 24 GB or more, CUDA 13.0 or newer, and not a V100 (CUDA 13 dropped it). An L40S (48 GB) runs every app 24 GB or more, CUDA 13: the link opens Search with these filters set. Sort by price 
 3. Storage Add volume → Volume disk , 60 GB at /workspace : the deploy page does not add it by itself 60 GB, already in the template 
 4. Open it Logs: Freefield is ready on RunPod , with the link and its passcode View instance logs → Refresh: a trycloudflare.com link with its passcode 
 5. When you are done Terminate the pod Destroy the instance 

The link comes in a few minutes (the image, then ComfyUI); the models keep downloading inside the studio, and each app
works as soon as its files are in. When a model asks you to accept its license on Hugging Face, the studio says which
one and takes your token in its Models panel, with no restart; the same panel downloads more packs. Anyone with the
link can use your GPU, so share it only with people you trust. Other packs, a volume that outlives the pod, and what to do when something fails are in
the guide.

Both are referral links. They cost you nothing: RunPod and Vast.ai give Freefield a share of the credits, which pays for
the lab's GPU runs.

 On your own PC in one line

Windows with an NVIDIA card (24 GB for most apps, RTX 20 series or newer). Open PowerShell and paste:

 

 start.ps1 does the rest, and asks nothing in the console:

- It checks the GPU and its driver (CUDA 13), and Docker Desktop,
 which it offers to install with winget when it is missing.
- It opens the studio in your browser while the default packs download (64 apps, 22.9 GB, once): the studio shows how
 it goes.
- As on RunPod and Vast.ai, the studio asks for your Hugging Face token when a model needs one: its Models panel lists
 the licenses to accept and takes the token. The same panel downloads more packs.
- The studio offers a desktop icon for next time. Each start picks up a new version of Freefield.

Press Enter in its window to stop Freefield and free the GPU.

Keep Docker Desktop's disk on an SSD: it holds the models, and they load from it. On a 3090 Ti the first Create Image
(with Expand my prompt ) took 32 s with the disk on an NVMe SSD and 9 min 25 s on a hard disk, almost all of it loading
models; the sampling itself was 5 s. The launcher warns when the disk is on a hard disk; Docker Desktop moves it in
Settings → Resources → Advanced → Disk image location.

Under the hood it is the same docker run as on a rented GPU (guide),
with the studio on 127.0.0.1 only and the models in the freefield volume. $env:FREEFIELD PACKS picks other packs
before you run it. powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Freefield\start.ps1" uninstall removes it
all; stop and logs work the same way. If Freefield closes while it loads a model, Docker ran out of RAM (by default
it gets half of yours): put [wsl2] and memory=40GB on two lines in %UserProfile%\.wslconfig , run wsl --shutdown 
and start it again.

 Status

 
 --- --- 
 Apps 120: 119 ready (39 apps with a workflow of their own, the 5 IC-LoRA apps ( genjutsu , reframe , sdr-hdr , mixed-media , dub ), morph , 72 template apps (a fixed prompt over one of those pipelines, written by tools/template apps.py ) and 2 model-free smoke apps) and moss-image as a draft. The 118 that use models each have a lab example made on a GPU 
 Open weights No API or partner nodes. Every model is a file you download, listed in its app's app.json with its Hugging Face repo, size and license; the cloud text-encoder branch of Lightricks' examples is removed 
 Workflows Built from official sources by tools/build apps.py (ComfyUI's templates, Lightricks' ComfyUI-LTXVideo examples, Comfy's comfy-reshoot ); the template apps reuse those bases and the two smoke apps are hand-written. tools/import wo
